title: Account CUDA scatter staging in VRAM admission and fail closed on OOM
finding: The first CUDA Boolean probe admitted work from a dense-resident-set estimate that omitted the temporary int64 row/column scatter-index tensors used while converting canonical CSR support to dense CUDA matrices. An allocator OOM could also escape as an exception instead of becoming explicit blocked experimental evidence.

change.device_memory_estimate: Count padded dense A/B/C plus Boolean support mask and one live pair of int64 scatter-index tensors. The two input blocks are packed sequentially, so only one staging pair is admitted at peak.
change.workspace_headroom: Keep the existing min(explicit-case-VRAM-ceiling, half-currently-free-VRAM) rule because cuBLAS workspace is implementation-owned and not exactly predictable by the probe.
change.oom_semantics: Translate only PyTorch's explicit OutOfMemoryError into status=blocked, claim=none, reason=cuda-out-of-memory. Unrelated exceptions remain visible and are re-raised.
change.authority: No production backend, runtime dependency, store, registry, scheduler, semantic plane or promotion path was added.

verification.gpu_execution: not executed on hosted runners and not claimed

acceptance: the explicit admission estimate includes CUDA scatter staging memory in addition to padded dense resident allocations
the estimate remains bounded by the existing TypedRelationBlock entry ceiling and probe case limits
an explicit PyTorch CUDA OOM becomes non-authorizing blocked evidence
a non-OOM runtime error is not swallowed or relabeled as an OOM
the existing deterministic Boolean CPU oracle contract remains executable and green on the exact tested head
no GPU speed, memory, Tensor-Core-use or benchmark-superiority claim is emitted

branch_hygiene.note: Only the existing exp/tensor-kernel-contract-01 line was advanced. No ref was created, deleted, renamed, force-updated or moved into the archive anchor.
